title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 342 (Prosecution of delinquent officers and members of company)

content.overview: If it appears to the Tribunal in the course of a winding up by the Tribunal that any person who is or has been an officer, or any member, of the company has been guilty of any offence in relation to the company, the Tribunal may, either on the application of any person interested in the winding up or suo motu, direct the liquidator to prosecute the offender or to refer the matter to the Registrar. When prosecution is instituted, the liquidator and every officer and agent of the company must give all reasonable assistance.
content.glance: In Tribunal winding up, Tribunal may direct prosecution of delinquent officers/members or referral to Registrar; duty to assist prosecution.
content.study: Section 342 provides the prosecution trigger in Tribunal winding up. If it appears that an officer or member has been guilty of an offence in relation to the company, the Tribunal may, on application or of its own motion, direct the liquidator to prosecute or to refer the matter to the Registrar. When prosecution is instituted, the liquidator and every person who is or has been an officer or agent of the company must give all assistance reasonably able to be given. ‘Agent’ includes banker, legal adviser and auditor. (Note: sub-sections relating to voluntary winding-up reporting were omitted by the IBC; the operative core for Tribunal winding up remains.)

sections.heading: Tribunal direction
sections.body: Tribunal may direct liquidator to prosecute or refer to Registrar where officer or member appears guilty of an offence relating to the company.

sections.heading: Duty to assist
sections.body: Liquidator, officers and agents must give all reasonable assistance in the prosecution.

provisions.title: Prosecution of delinquent officers and members of company

examples.title: Referral for prosecution
examples.body: During Tribunal winding up evidence emerges that a former director falsified books. The Tribunal directs the liquidator under s. 342 to refer the matter to the Registrar for prosecution.

hypotheticals.question: Must the Tribunal wait for an application before directing prosecution?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The Tribunal may act suo motu as well as on the application of any person interested in the winding up.

misconceptions.trap: Prosecution under s. 342 is automatic once an offence appears.
misconceptions.correction: The Tribunal has a discretion to direct prosecution or referral; it is not automatic.
